title: Redbank Dam & Waterworks Gully
lede: A quick out-and-back walk or run from the old Redbank Dam, up Waterworks Gully into Avisford Nature Reserve.
description: A 7.5 km return walk on fire trail and single track from the old Redbank Dam on Old Reservoir Road, Mudgee, up Waterworks Gully into Avisford Nature Reserve. Quick enough for before or after work.

card.blurb: Up Waterworks Gully from the old Redbank Dam and back. A quick walk or run on fire trail, before or after work.

facts.label: Walk type
facts.value: Fire trail and single track; Return

facts.label: Highlights
facts.value: The old Redbank Dam, Waterworks Gully, orchids in spring

intro: Redbank Dam was once part of Mudgee's water supply. It's been deconstructed and no longer holds water, but it makes a good starting point for a walk up Waterworks Gully into Avisford Nature Reserve. It's mostly fire trail, about 275 m of climbing all up, and quick enough to walk or run before or after work.

getting_there.intro: The walk starts at the entrance to Avisford Nature Reserve at Redbank Dam, on Old Reservoir Road on the south-western edge of Mudgee.

options.heading: Old Reservoir Road
options.text: Take Old Reservoir Road and park at the Avisford Nature Reserve entrance at Redbank Dam. Head through the gate onto the fire trail.

getting_there.note: Avisford Nature Reserve is managed by NSW National Parks, so stay on the tracks.

walk_intro:
The route heads out on the fire trail past the old Redbank Dam, follows Waterworks Gully west, then climbs out of the gully on the Waterworks Gully Trail into the hills of Avisford Nature Reserve. It's about 3.8 km each way. Come back the same way, and finish on the single track along the north side of the old dam.

For a short walk of about 2 km, go up the fire trail past the dam and come straight back on the single track on the north side.

stops.heading: Redbank Dam
stops.text: Go through the gate onto the fire trail. The first section takes you past Redbank Dam, an old water supply for Mudgee. It's been deconstructed so it doesn't hold any water now. There are picnic tables and signs around the dam to check out, and you can walk along the base of the dam.

stops.heading: Waterworks Gully
stops.text: Past the dam, the fire trail follows Waterworks Gully west into Avisford Nature Reserve, winding up the gully between the spurs. Keep an eye out for orchids in spring.

stops.heading: Waterworks Gully Trail
stops.text: At the head of the gully the Waterworks Gully Trail swings south, then climbs west out of the gully towards the higher ridges of the reserve.

stops.heading: The turnaround
stops.text: The route turns around in the bush near the western edge of Avisford Nature Reserve. There's no view here, so just turn and head back the way you came.

stops.heading: Back past the dam
stops.text: Head back down the fire trail. It's downhill most of the way, so it makes a good run. Near the end, take the single track along the north side of the old dam back to the gate.

tips.heading: Navigation
tips.text: It's fire trail all the way, so navigation is straightforward. Carry a map or the GPX on your phone.

tips.heading: Nature reserve
tips.text: Avisford Nature Reserve is managed by NSW National Parks. Stay on the tracks and leave the gate as you found it.

tips.heading: Water
tips.text: Carry the water you'll need, especially on a hot day.

tips.heading: Respect the Country
tips.text: This is Wiradjuri Country. Look, but don't touch. Leave no trace.
